title: What is the difference between transaction isolation levels and optimistic/pessimistic concurrency control?

From what I understand, depending on the isolation level selected (e.g., Read Committed, Repeatable Read, Serializable), different types of locking might be applied to prevent concurrency problems between transactions. At the same time, there are optimistic and pessimistic concurrency control strategies, which also seem to define different approaches to locking and conflict handling. This is where my confusion begins: Are transaction isolation levels and optimistic/pessimistic concurrency control fundamentally different concepts? Are they just different ways of managing concurrency? Or are they complementary concepts, where one operates at a different abstraction level than the other? For example, if I select a specific isolation level, does that already imply a certain concurrency control strategy?
